'''Jane Maienschein''' (born September 23, 1950) is an American professor and director of the Center for Biology and Society at [[Arizona State University]].

==Early life and education==
Maienschein was born on September 23, 1950.<ref>{{Cite web |date=August 4, 2025 |title=Maienschein, Jane |url=https://id.loc.gov/authorities/names/n85171188.html |access-date=June 12, 2026 |website=Library of Congress}}</ref> She was admitted to the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]], but transferred to [[Yale University]] in 1969, where she was a member of [[Manuscript Society (Yale University)|Manuscript Society]]. In 1972, she graduated with honors in History, the Arts, and Letters. She then attended [[Indiana University Bloomington]] to conduct her Ph.D work. 

Her mentor, Dr. Frederick Churchill, was interested in historical embryological research. She was awarded a fellowship at the [[Smithsonian]], to study the history of microscopy. The [[National Science Foundation]] provided funding for her dissertation. Maienschein joined the [[Marine Biological Laboratory]] in Woods Hole, Massachusetts, to research historical [[embryology]], [[morphogenesis]], and [[cellular differentiation]]. She researched the history and philosophy of [[developmental biology]] and issues surrounding [[stem cell]] research and [[regenerative medicine]].<ref name="hdl.handle">Embryo Project Encyclopedia Editorial Team, "Jane Maienschein", 2008, "[http://hdl.handle.net/2286/embryo:125546]", December 22, 2010</ref>

==Work==
Maienschein focuses on the social, political, and legal contexts of scientific research and is currently the director of the Center for Biology and Society at Arizona State University, which states the goal of "promoting exploration of conceptual foundations and historical development of the biosciences and their diverse interactions with society".<ref>ASU Center for Biology and Society, "Programs in Biology and Society", 2010, "[http://cbs.asu.edu/programs/index.php] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110311160432/http://cbs.asu.edu/programs/index.php|date=2011-03-11}}", December 22, 2010</ref>  To quote the CBS, "We engage in activities across multiple disciplines that allow opportunities for intellectual ferment and increased impact by creating research and educational collaborations and communication." Maienschein and colleague Manfred Laubichler are particularly interested in [[evolutionary developmental biology]]. The School of Life Sciences has received millions of dollars from the [[Howard Hughes Medical Institute]] to develop the [[School of Life Sciences (Central South University)|School of Life Sciences]] Undergraduate Research (SOLUR) program, a research program. Maienschein served as the first president for the [[International Society for the History, Philosophy, and Social Studies of Biology]] in 1989–1991 and served as president of the [[History of Science Society]]. She is director of [[The Embryo Project Encyclopedia]], along with Dr. Manfred Laubichler.<ref name="hdl.handle" /> This project, along with her other work in embryonic research, gives context to greater political, philosophical, and existential debates on what constitutes human life.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Maienschein |first=Jane |title=Embryos under the Microscope: The Diverging Meanings of Life |date=2014 |publisher=Harvard University Press |isbn=978-0-674-72555-3 |edition=Pilot project. eBook available to selected US libraries only |location=Cambridge, MA}}</ref>

==Recognition==
Maienschein is Regents' Professor and President's Professor at [[Arizona State University]]'s School of Life Sciences.<ref name="asunews">[http://asunews.asu.edu/20101118_USProfAZ Professor named Top in Arizona, Recognized Nationally], Arizona State University (November 19, 2010).</ref> In 2000, Maienschein received the Joseph H. Hazen Education Prize from the [[History of Science Society]],<ref>[https://hssonline.org/about/honors/joseph-h-hazen-education-prize/ Joseph H. Hazen Education Prize], History of Science Society.</ref> and in 2024 she received the History of Science Society's highest honor, the [[George Sarton Medal]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |date=July 10, 2024 |title=2024 Sarton Medalist: Jane Maienschein |url=https://hssonline.org/blogpost/1987463/502761/2024-Sarton-Medalist-Jane-Maienschein |access-date=November 23, 2022 |website=History of Science Society}}</ref>

Maienschein has created the Biology and Society; Bioethics, Policy, and Law; The History and Philosophy of Science; Ecology, Economics, Ethics and Environment; The Embryo Project Encyclopedia, ASU's Bioethics in Films Series, Responsible Conduct in Research and the History of Biology projects held at the [[Marine Biological Laboratory]].<ref name="asunews"/> She is also the first president of the [[International Society for the History, Philosophy, and Social Studies of Biology]] (ISHPSSB).<ref>{{cite web |title=In Memory of David Hull: Reflections delivered at the 2011 Biennial meeting of ISHPSSB by his friends and colleagues Jane Maienschein, Robert J. Richards, and Christopher D. Horvath |url=https://www.ishpssb.org/news/newsletters/37-newsletter-volume-23-no-1-issue-43-fall-2011}}</ref>

Maienschein is a fellow of the [[Association for Women in Science]] (AWIS) and the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]] (AAAS), has served two terms as a board member for national AWIS in Washington, D.C and served on the board of directors of AAAS.<ref name=":0" /> She has published over 20 articles and several books as shown on her CV.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Jane Maienschein {{!}} School of Life Sciences|url=https://sols.asu.edu/jane-maienschein|access-date=2021-01-15|website=sols.asu.edu|language=en}}</ref> She was published in [[the Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy]] on "[[Epigenesis (biology)|Epigenesis]] and [[Preformation]]". Maienschein wrote "Whose View of Life?: Embryos, Cloning, and Stem Cells". Maienschein and Manfred Laubichler collaborated to co-write: "From Embryology to Evo-Devo: A History of Developmental Evolution"<ref>{{Cite book|title=From embryology to evo-devo : a history of developmental evolution|date=2007|publisher=MIT Press|others=Laubichler, Manfred Dietrich., Maienschein, Jane.|isbn=978-0-262-27797-6|location=Cambridge, Mass.|oclc=123177551}}</ref> and Form and Function in Developmental Evolution.<ref>{{Cite book|title=Form and function in developmental evolution|date=2009|publisher=Cambridge University Press|others=Laubichler, Manfred Dietrich., Maienschein, Jane.|isbn=978-0-511-50844-8|location=Cambridge, UK|oclc=368415550}}</ref>

In 2009, Maienschein presented, with [[TEDx Talks|Tedx Talks]], on "Stem Cells, Regenerative Medicine and Us". In November 2010, Maienschein was named the 2010 Arizona Professor of the Year, by the [[Carnegie Foundation for the Advancement of Teaching]] and the [[Council for Advancement and Support of Education]].<ref name="asunews" />
